analyzed_vuln.description: `labelRecursivePatterns()` maintains a manual parse stack (`state`) for parentheses/`$(` recursion markers, but it unconditionally executes `state.back()`/`state.pop_back()` on every `')'`. If input has more closing parentheses than the function’s tracked opens (possible with malformed SMARTS from `M  MRV SMA`), the stack can be popped down to empty and then accessed again, corrupting `std::list` internals and leading to an invalid free in `std::list::pop_back()` (ASan bad-free on stack address). Root cause is missing balance/emptiness validation before stack pop, not allocator code.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Fuzzer path: `MolDataStreamToMol` -> `ParseV2000CTAB` -> `ParseMolBlockProperties` -> `ParseMarvinSmartsLine` -> `SmartsToMol` -> `labelRecursivePatterns`. A mol block containing an `M  MRV SMA` property with malformed SMARTS (especially unbalanced `)` relative to tracked `(` / `$(` recursion state) triggers the bug during recursive-pattern relabeling before normal SMARTS parse error handling. No special heap grooming needed; parser just needs to reach this Marvin SMARTS line with crafted text.
